subject: Mistral bridge variant onboarding + pin coordination
messages:
From: Olivia Harris <olivia@mistral.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: mistral-eng@lists.mistral.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: Mistral bridge variant for Redwood catalog

Hey Sean —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Mistral shipped a bridge variant (mistral-bridge-v1.7b) that we think will be a good fit for low-latency edge tiers. We put together a short spec and compatibility checklist (attached).

Primary asks:
- Onboard the variant into Redwood’s catalog as a compatible serving variant.
- Pining guidance: we’d like a short-lived version pin (2–4 weeks) during early traffic shaping while telemetry heats up.
- Multi-region routing: recommend an initial US-only rollout with canary in us-west-2.

Key constraints: the variant uses a slightly different tokenizer behavior for a subset of special tokens (we documented a migration flag in the checklist). We will support a fallback model variant if Redwood needs to keep behavior consistent.

Can you loop in product and infra folks to confirm feasibility and expected telemetry surface?

Attached: mistral-bridge-specs.pdf, mistral-v1.7b-checklist.csv

Thanks — happy to run a 30-min sync if that helps.

—Olivia Harris
Program Manager, Model Partnerships
Mistral Labs

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Olivia Harris <olivia@mistral.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: Mistral bridge variant for Redwood catalog

Marissa / Dev / Laura —

Looping you all in on a Mistral variant ask. Quick summary:
- External: mistral-bridge-v1.7b, want a short pin during initial traffic shaping (2–4 weeks).
- Risk: tokenizer edge-case flagged in checklist; Mistral proposes an internal fallback variant.
- Product asks: how does this affect catalog UX and rollback/runbook expectations?

Please reply with: (1) product acceptability (can we ship pinned for a short window), (2) infra constraints for a canary in us-west-2, and (3) telemetry/events we need to validate quality/regression.

Olivia — thanks for the doc. We’ll review and propose a concrete plan in 24 hours.

Thanks,
Sean
Head of Partnerships (inbox)
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Olivia Harris <olivia@mistral.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: Mistral bridge variant for Redwood catalog

Thanks Sean — quick product take:

1) Short pin window OK if we get:
   - explicit migration flag documented (looks present)
   - a canary plan with traffic thresholds and automated rollback triggers (e.g., latency + generation-quality regression > predefined delta).

2) UX: We should expose the variant as "beta" in the catalog and annotate tokenizer behavior in the model docs. Avoid automatic traffic shifts for customers on pinned versions — they should opt into the variant.

3) Telemetry & evals: Need these signals from infra/eng:
   - per-request tokenization failure rate (new special-token errors)
   - delta on median latency at p50/p95 during identical prompts
   - regression scoring on a small eval prompt set (we’ll provide ~150 seed prompts)

Ask: Dev, can infra emit tokenization error counts and per-model eval score snapshots to the metrics pipeline within the canary window? Also, if we're pinning for 2–4 weeks, we need a simple way to automatically unpin at expiry unless product approves extension.

I can draft the catalog blurb and the customer-facing docs once we confirm telemetry.

—Marissa
Product Manager, Model Catalog
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Olivia Harris <olivia@mistral.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: Mistral bridge variant for Redwood catalog

Quick infra status and feasibility notes:

1) Canary routing: we can do region-limited canary in us-west-2 and a manual traffic ramp. I recommend starting at 0.5% of platform requests for the first 12 hours, then step to 2% for 24h if no regressions.

2) Pin mechanics: we support time-bound pins. I’ll create an automatic expiry (2 weeks default) and a one-click extension flow for Product to approve another 2-week window. We’ll add a follow-up job to notify owners 48h before expiry.

3) Telemetry: We can emit tokenization errors (tagged as tokenizer.mistral_bridge.special_token_errors) and per-variant latency p50/p95. For eval snapshots, we can ingest Marissa’s 150 prompts into the eval pipeline and produce a daily regression report. Need the prompt set and expected scoring metric (BLEU / ROUGE / or custom embedding-similarity).

4) Fallback plan: if tokenizer failure rate > 0.1% OR eval-score regression > 3 points (configurable), automated rollback to the fallback variant will trigger and an incident will be opened.

Action items:
- Olivia: confirm the exact flag name for tokenization compatibility (so we can map logs).
- Marissa: share the 150 prompts and desired scoring metric.
- Sean: confirm who owns the extension decision and the kickoff meeting cadence.

I’ll open INF-2345 to track the infra work and attach the pin expiry automation PR once ready.

—Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
